newsitem.title: USA: Lock up sexual predators - Connecticut official.
newsitem.headline: Lock up sexual predators - Connecticut official.

text.p: Connecticut's top prosecutor said Tuesday he would seek legislation allowing the state to lock up sexual predators in mental hospitals even after they had served their prison terms.

"As a society we can no longer deal with the sexual predator as we do with other criminals," Chief State's Attorney John Bailey told a news conference. He said the bill, to be introduced in next year's state legislative session, would allow civil commitment of sexually violent predators.

He said the act was modelled on a Kansas law upheld by the U.S. Supreme Court in a controversial ruling last month. The court said states could confine sex offenders who had a "mental abnormality" and were likely to engage in "predatory acts of sexual violence" if released.
Some civil liberties advocates have said the ruling violates the traditional notion that people should be punished for past, not future, crimes.

Bailey said tougher laws were needed because the number of prisoners in the United States serving time for violent sexual assault had increased by 15 percent a year since 1980. He said similar laws were in effect in California, Arizona, Washington, Wisconsin, Kansas, New Jersey and New York.
